subject: Qur'an & Tajweed
source: Continues the school Drive Quran folder progression (TPS Quran Tracker tajweed rules Years 1-6) into KS3/KS4; classical tajweed (Hafs 'an 'Asim) and tadabbur method; Qur'an text per the Madinah mushaf

lessons.unit: Unit 1: Noon and meem - complete rules
lessons.title: Diagnostic: noon, meem and madd
objectives: Show recall of rules from KS2 and Year 7
Identify gaps with a diagnostic quiz

keywords.def: a check to find what you know and what to improve

starter: Bismillah. Recite the isti'adha and basmalah.
Name the four rules of noon sakinah and tanween with letters.
Name the types of madd lazim.

teach.heading: Why diagnose?
bullets: Recitation is a skill built over years
teach.note: Explain that Year 8 builds on all earlier learning. Ask: what has been your most secure rule? Which is least secure? Pupils note answers privately.

teach.heading: Quiz
teach.note: Run the quiz in a form or on paper. Questions include: which rule in مِن بَعْدِ? How many counts for الضَّالِّينَ? Tell pupils the purpose is learning, not marks.

teach.heading: Recite and spot
bullets: Mark each rule on a printed copy
teach.note: Pupils mark a printed Al-Fatihah with every rule. Check: the yaa in إِيَّاكَ carries a shaddah but no ghunnah, since ghunnah belongs to noon and meem. Discuss errors kindly and clarify.

teach.heading: Targets
bullets: Choose a surah to practise on
teach.note: Pupils write targets and a plan. Share a few. Close with a dua for steadfastness in learning the Qur'an.

practice: Which rule is in مِن بَعْدِ?
How many counts for madd lazim?
independent: Complete the diagnostic quiz
Mark the rules on Al-Fatihah
Write two targets and a plan
exit: Name one rule you are secure with.
What will you practise this week?
lessons.homework: Practise your two target rules daily with five examples each.
lessons.send: SEND/EAL: quiz with word bank and examples. Stretch: write extra quiz questions for the class.

lessons.unit: Unit 1: Noon and meem - complete rules
lessons.title: Noon sakinah and tanween: in depth
objectives: Group the ikhfa letters by makhraj
Explain idgham with and without ghunnah
Apply the rules to longer passages

keywords.def: clear noon in the same word before yaa or waaw

teach.heading: The ikhfa letters by strength
bullets: Heavy: ص ض ط ظ ق - fuller
Light: ت ث ج د ذ ز س ش ف ك
All with two counts of ghunnah
The mouth takes the shape of the next letter
teach.note: Explain that ikhfa is neither clear nor merged; the tongue does not touch its place. Demonstrate مِن قَبْلِ vs مِن شَرِّ. Pupils copy and listen.

teach.heading: Idgham in detail
bullets: With ghunnah: ي ن م و
Exception: same word - the noon stays clear
teach.note: Examples: مَن يَقُولُ, مِّن رَّبِّهِمْ, الدُّنْيَا, صِنْوَانٌ. Pupils say why each is read as it is. Misconception: ghunnah with laam and raa.

teach.heading: Tanween and noon alike
bullets: Mark the rule over the tanween
Stop at an end: rules do not apply
teach.note: Show خَيْرٌ لَّكَ and عَلِيمٌ حَكِيمٌ. If we stop on the tanween, there is no noon rule. Check with: هُدًى لِّلْمُتَّقِينَ.

teach.heading: Passage practice
teach.note: Use Al-Qadr: أَنزَلْنَاهُ (ikhfa), خَيْرٌ مِّنْ (idgham ghunnah), مِّن كُلِّ (ikhfa). Pupils label then recite. Praise good ghunnah length.

practice: Which rule applies in مِن قَبْلِ?
Why is الدُّنْيَا read with a clear noon?
independent: Label every noon and tanween in Al-Qadr
Sort 20 phrases by rule
Recite Al-Qadr and review with a partner
exit: Name the ikhfa letters that are heavy.
Give an example of idgham without ghunnah.
lessons.homework: Label every noon sakinah and tanween in a surah you are memorising.
lessons.send: SEND/EAL: rule chart with colours. Stretch: find all four rules in 10 ayat.

lessons.unit: Unit 1: Noon and meem - complete rules
lessons.title: Meem sakinah and ghunnah in detail
objectives: State the three rules of meem sakinah
starter: Name the three rules of meem sakinah.

teach.heading: The three rules
teach.note: Revise from Year 2. Make a quick table on the board. Pupils give examples. Remind pupils that the rules involve the lips.

teach.heading: Examples
teach.note: Al-Baqarah 2:249 and Al-Fil. Pupils recite each and describe what happens to the lips. For ikhfa, the lips hardly touch; for idgham, they join.

teach.heading: Extra care
bullets: Izhar before و and ف: do not hide the meem
teach.note: The lips must not blend into the waaw or faa. Pupils practise عَلَيْهِمْ وَلَا (Al-Fatihah, meem before waaw) and then find a meem before faa in the mushaf.

teach.heading: Ghunnah mushaddad
teach.note: Revise the highest level of ghunnah. Pupils recite words such as ثُمَّ and إِنَّ from the surahs. Take care to keep ghunnah steady and not too long.

practice: Which rule is used before baa?
How long is ghunnah on a letter with shaddah?
independent: Label all meem sakinah in Al-Fil and At-Takathur
Pair quiz on the three meem rules
Record yourself reciting Al-Fil
exit: Name the three meem rules.
What happens to the lips in idgham shafawi?
lessons.homework: Label every meem sakinah in Al-Fil and recite it with correct lip movement.
lessons.send: SEND/EAL: lip diagrams and colour keys. Stretch: find meem sakinah rules in Surat Al-Baqarah 1-5.

lessons.title: Identical, close and same-place letters

keywords.def: two letters from the same makhraj but different qualities

teach.heading: When letters meet
bullets: The first letter merges into the second
teach.note: Introduce the situation: a sukoon letter followed by a letter that is the same, close or from the same place. Ask pupils what they think happens.

teach.heading: Mithlayn: identical
bullets: The baa merges into the baa
Reads as one baa with shaddah
teach.note: Say the phrase slowly then at pace. Pupils hear a single doubled baa. Other examples exist, e.g. in وَقَد دَّخَلُوا the dals merge.

teach.heading: Mutajanisayn: same place
teach.note: Daal and taa come from the same place. The first is voiced; the second whispered. The daal merges completely. Pupils recite and compare.

teach.heading: Mutaqaribayn: close
bullets: Qaaf and kaaf; laam and raa
teach.note: Explain that qaaf and kaaf are close; laam and raa are close. Merge fully. Pupils note the shaddah that is written. Practise slowly.

practice: Which type is اضْرِب بِّعَصَاكَ?
What happens to the daal in قَد تَّبَيَّنَ?
independent: Sort 8 phrases into the three types
Read them with merging
Create a chart with the rules and examples
exit: What does mithlayn mean?
Give one example of mutaqaribayn.
lessons.homework: Read the four examples every day and explain each to a family member.
lessons.send: SEND/EAL: chart with examples and audio. Stretch: find more examples in the mushaf.

lessons.title: Waqf and ibtida': four types of stop
objectives: Name the four types of waqf
Choose good places to stop and start

keywords.def: a complete stop - the meaning is finished
a sufficient stop - connected in meaning
a good stop, but start again from earlier
a poor stop which spoils the meaning

starter: Name the stopping signs in the mushaf.
How do you stop on a word with ة?

teach.heading: Why stopping matters
bullets: Stopping in the wrong place can change meaning
The Qur'an is clear and we protect it
Scholars set out rules for stopping
teach.note: Introduce with the example of stopping at لَا تَقْرَبُوا الصَّلَاةَ (4:43) before وَأَنتُمْ سُكَارَىٰ: the meaning would be 'do not approach the prayer', which is wrong. Pupils explain why it is a poor stop.

teach.heading: Four types
teach.note: Give a simple explanation of each. Tamm: no link to what follows. Kafi: connected in meaning but separate grammatically. Hasan: sentence is fine but connected to what follows. Qabih: breaks the meaning.

teach.heading: Starting again
bullets: Begin where the meaning is sound
Do not begin on half a word
teach.note: If you run out of breath at a poor place, go back to a good starting place. Model with a long ayah. Pupils practise with Al-Ma'un.

teach.heading: Using the signs
bullets: Follow signs in the Madinah mushaf
Take a breath at ayah ends
teach.note: Pupils read a page with signs. Teacher checks. Mention that stopping at the end of an ayah is the preferred practice for beginners.

practice: Why is stopping at لَا تَقْرَبُوا الصَّلَاةَ a poor stop?
What is waqf tamm?
independent: Mark stops on a printed Al-Ma'un
Classify four stops as good or poor with reasons
Recite a passage with correct waqf
exit: Name the four types of waqf.
What should you do if you run out of breath at a poor place?
lessons.homework: Read a page of the mushaf with correct stops and breaths.
lessons.send: SEND/EAL: sign flash cards and examples. Stretch: explain why starting matters as much as stopping.

lessons.title: Waqf in practice: stopping on different endings
objectives: Know that roum and ishmam exist and are learned with a teacher
Recite a long ayah with good breath
starter: How do we stop on tanween fathah?
How do we stop on round ة?

teach.heading: Rules for stopping
bullets: Tanween kasrah or dammah: drop it
teach.note: Model each. Examples: رَحِيمًا to 'raheema'; أَحَدٌ to 'ahad'; الْمِسْكِينِ unchanged; رَحْمَةٌ to 'rahmah'. Pupils practise on words from the mushaf.

teach.heading: With madd
teach.note: Revise madd 'arid. Pupils recite the end of each ayah of Al-Fatihah with 4 counts. Explain that the choice of length is your teacher's guidance.

teach.heading: Echo and heavy letters
bullets: Stopping on heavy letters: keep full
teach.note: Pupils practise the echo on stopped words. Heavy letters at the end keep their fullness. Do not add a vowel. Pairs give feedback.

teach.heading: Long ayat
bullets: Look ahead to find a breath point
teach.note: Use Al-Ma'un as a practice text. Where can we breathe in ayat 5-7? Choose points that suit the meaning. Teacher gives guidance.

practice: How do you stop on تَوَّابًا?
What happens to ة when stopping?
independent: Write the stopped form of 10 words
Recite Al-Fatihah stopping at every ayah
Mark breath points on Al-Ma'un
exit: How do you stop on a word with tanween kasrah?
What do we do with madd when stopping?
lessons.homework: Record yourself stopping at each ayah of a surah you know and listen for errors.
lessons.send: SEND/EAL: table with stopped forms. Stretch: explain how stopping affects qalqalah.

lessons.unit: Unit 4: Surah study - Al-Ma'un and At-Takathur
lessons.title: Surat Al-Ma'un: reading and rules
starter: Name the four types of waqf.
Which rule is used for tanween before laam?

teach.heading: Ayat 1-3
teach.note: Meaning: Have you seen the one who denies the judgement? That is the one who pushes away the orphan and does not urge the feeding of the poor. Chunk and echo.

teach.heading: Ayat 4-7
teach.note: Meaning: so woe to those who pray, who are heedless of their prayer, who show off, and who withhold small kindnesses. Chunk and echo. Explain that the prayer must be sincere and joined with kindness.

teach.heading: Tajweed
bullets: عَن صَلَاتِهِمْ - ikhfa with heavy Saad
teach.note: Pupils label each. Notice the heavy Saad after ikhfa. Check the natural madd in سَاهُونَ and مَاعُونَ. Compare ayat 5 and 6, which start the same.

teach.heading: Memorise
teach.note: Use chaining and link the repeated phrase الَّذِينَ هُمْ. Test aloud with a partner. Assess with the rubric.

practice: Recite Al-Ma'un ayah 1.
Which rule is in فَوَيْلٌ لِّلْمُصَلِّينَ?
independent: Label tajweed rules on a printed Al-Ma'un
Memorise ayat 1-3
Recite individually
exit: Name one rule in ayah 5.
What does ayah 3 tell us to do?
lessons.homework: Recite Al-Ma'un daily and learn ayat 1-3 by heart.
lessons.send: SEND/EAL: chunked audio and translation. Stretch: learn the whole surah.

lessons.unit: Unit 4: Surah study - Al-Ma'un and At-Takathur
lessons.title: Surat Al-Ma'un: tadabbur
objectives: Explain the main themes of Al-Ma'un
Use the four questions method for tadabbur

teach.heading: Belief and kindness
bullets: Denying the judgement leads to harshness
teach.note: Discuss the link between ayah 1 and ayat 2-3. The surah connects belief in the Day of Judgement with the treatment of orphans and the poor. Ask: how does belief change behaviour?

teach.heading: Sincere prayer
bullets: Allah wants prayer with focus and sincerity
teach.note: Explain gently: the surah warns against heedlessness and showing off. We should check our intentions. Ask: how can we pray with focus?

teach.heading: Small kindnesses
teach.note: Scholars mention that al-ma'un includes small items of everyday help. Pupils give examples: lending a pencil, holding a door, giving a tissue. Ask: which can you do tomorrow?

teach.heading: Action plan
teach.note: Pupils write an action plan: what, when, and for whom. Share some. Close with a dua asking Allah to make us sincere.

practice: What is al-ma'un?
Why does the surah mention the orphan and the poor?
independent: Answer the four tadabbur questions on ayat 1-3
Write an action plan with three kindnesses
Recite Al-Ma'un to a partner
exit: Name one theme of the surah.
What will you do this week?
lessons.homework: Do one small kindness each day this week and record it.
lessons.send: SEND/EAL: sentence frames for reflection. Stretch: write a short essay on belief and behaviour.

lessons.unit: Unit 4: Surah study - Al-Ma'un and At-Takathur
lessons.title: Surat At-Takathur: reading and rules

teach.heading: Ayat 1-4
teach.note: Meaning: competing for more distracts you until you visit the graves. No! You will know. Again, no! You will know. Chunk and echo. Note ghunnah on ثُمَّ.

teach.heading: Ayat 5-8
teach.note: Meaning: if you knew with certainty, you would surely see the Hellfire, then you will see it with certain sight, then you will be asked about the blessings. Present the surah as a gentle wake-up call, not a threat.

teach.heading: Tajweed
teach.note: Pupils label rules. The laam of التَّكَاثُرُ merges into the taa. The noon with shaddah in لَتَرَوُنَّ is ghunnah. Practise the madd letters and counts.

teach.heading: Memorise
teach.note: Use chaining and link patterns. Note the repeated كَلَّا and ثُمَّ. Test in pairs and give feedback using the rubric.

practice: Recite At-Takathur ayah 1.
Where is ghunnah in the surah?
independent: Label rules in At-Takathur
Memorise ayat 1-4
Recite individually
exit: What distracts people in ayah 1?
Name one rule in ayah 7.
lessons.homework: Recite At-Takathur daily and learn ayat 1-4 by heart.
lessons.send: SEND/EAL: chunked audio and translation. Stretch: learn the whole surah.

lessons.unit: Unit 4: Surah study - Al-Ma'un and At-Takathur
lessons.title: At-Takathur: tadabbur and gratitude

teach.heading: Competing for more
teach.note: Ask pupils what people compete for today. Avoid judgement of individuals. Link to the surah's gentle warning that distraction ends at death.

teach.heading: Certainty
teach.note: The surah moves from knowing for sure to seeing for sure. Discuss: when we are certain about something, how do we behave? Link to why belief in the Day of Judgement shapes our actions.

teach.heading: Blessings
bullets: We will be asked about blessings
teach.note: The meaning is that we will be asked about the blessings Allah gave us. Pupils list blessings in groups: health, family, time, knowledge. Ask: how do we show shukr?

teach.heading: Reflection
teach.note: Pupils write a short reflection with these three items and recite the surah. Close with a dua for gratitude and focus.

practice: Recite At-Takathur.
What will we be asked about?
independent: Write a reflection of 6-8 sentences
Recite At-Takathur to a partner
Make a gratitude list of 10 blessings
exit: What does the surah warn about?
Name one way to show shukr.
lessons.homework: Write and recite one gratitude dua each day this week.
lessons.send: SEND/EAL: sentence frames and word bank. Stretch: write a short khutbah-style talk on the surah.

lessons.unit: Unit 4: Surah study - Al-Ma'un and At-Takathur
lessons.title: Long-term memorisation: revision cycles
starter: Name the three layers of revision.

teach.heading: Why we forget
teach.note: Draw a forgetting curve. Pupils discuss why we revise. Use a simple analogy: watering a plant. Refer to the idea that the Qur'an must be revised regularly.

teach.heading: A weekly cycle
teach.note: Pupils create a weekly plan with their surahs. Review how long each takes. Make it short and realistic.

teach.heading: Test one another
teach.note: Practise the start-continue game with Al-Ma'un and At-Takathur. Pupils note where they hesitate. Praise honest feedback.

teach.heading: Dua and sincerity
teach.note: Close with a dua. Remind pupils that memory is a gift from Allah and that effort, consistency and sincerity matter.

practice: Recite Al-Ma'un ayah 1.
Name one thing that helps you revise.
independent: Write a four-week revision plan
Test a partner on two surahs
Record yourself reciting two surahs from memory
exit: What is spaced repetition?
Name two layers in your plan.
lessons.homework: Follow your revision plan and tick off each day.
lessons.send: SEND/EAL: visual planner and audio. Stretch: design a revision game.

lessons.unit: Unit 4: Surah study - Al-Ma'un and At-Takathur
lessons.title: Recital assessment and reflection
objectives: Recite a chosen surah with the rubric
starter: Name the criteria on the rubric.
Choose a surah for your recital.

teach.heading: Prepare
teach.note: Give pupils five minutes to prepare quietly. Remind them of adab: wudu if possible, a calm place, a dua. Reduce nervousness with encouragement.

teach.heading: Recite
teach.note: Pupils recite individually or in breakout pairs. Teacher or partner uses the rubric. Keep the atmosphere supportive.

teach.heading: Feedback
teach.note: Provide feedback in the format of the rubric. Pupils note down. Ask them to compare with their baseline.

teach.heading: Reflect
teach.note: Pupils write a short reflection. Share one thing aloud. Close with a dua for steadfastness and sincerity.

practice: Which rule is most secure for you?
Which rule needs more practice?
independent: Recite your chosen surah for assessment
Complete peer feedback
Write a reflection and three targets
exit: Name one strength.
Name one target.
lessons.homework: Practise your targets daily and record a new recitation next week.
lessons.send: SEND/EAL: simplified rubric and word bank. Stretch: peer-coach another pupil.
